description: Never interpolate raw user input directly into SQL queries — use bound parameters
Do not hard-code secrets, API keys or passwords in source; load them from a secret manager at runtime
Avoid eval/exec or dynamic code execution on data that may be user-controlled
Validate and bound the size of every external input before parsing it
Never log tokens, passwords or full request bodies
Use constant-time comparison when checking signatures or tokens
Disable TLS certificate verification only in tests — never in production code paths
Do not swallow exceptions with a bare except or empty catch block; handle, narrow or re-raise
Always check and handle returned errors instead of discarding them
Close files, sockets and database connections deterministically (with/try-with-resources/defer)
Guard against division by zero and empty collections before computing averages
Avoid mutable default arguments; they are shared across calls
Compare floating-point money values with a tolerance or use a decimal type
Cache repeated database lookups inside the request loop
Batch database queries instead of issuing one query per item (N+1 queries)
Avoid quadratic membership checks on lists in hot loops; use a set or dict
Stream large files instead of reading them fully into memory
Reuse HTTP clients and connection pools rather than creating one per request
Do not start an unbounded goroutine or thread per incoming item; use a worker pool
Keep I/O at the edges: business rules should not construct database or HTTP clients directly
Depend on interfaces for external services so they can be substituted in tests
Avoid global mutable state shared across requests
A function should do one thing; split functions that validate
Propagate cancellation and timeouts (context/deadline) through every outbound call
Replace magic numbers and strings with named constants
Functions longer than about 50 lines usually hide several responsibilities
Remove commented-out code; version control keeps history
Use precise types instead of any/Object/interface{} at module boundaries
Resolve TODO and FIXME markers or track them in the issue tracker
Avoid single-character variable names — they hurt readability
Use consistent naming conventions for the language (snake_case / camelCase)
Keep lines under 100–120 characters
